title: UPDATE: Gemma 4 Model Reaches 125,000 Tokens per Second Prefill Using Resin Tool

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
A developer used the Resin environment and an Astra agent to push the processing speed of Google's gemma-4-E2B-it model to new levels on an Nvidia A100 GPU. The setup achieved a prefill throughput of 125,000 tokens per second (tok/s) per GPU and a decode rate of 4,000 tok/s per GPU, allowing for a delivery speed of 130 tok/s per user.

The configuration was built from scratch in four hours, featuring low-batch decode optimizations such as fusing Triton and cuBLAS GELU kernels and stripping assistant key-value caches to reduce latency from 12ms to 1ms. These results surpass Google's reported benchmark for the same model, where the use of Gemini 4 Argon and vLLM reached a throughput of 108,000 tok/s.

Speeding up Gemma!

Gemini 4 Argon enabled a 2.85x speedup on an A100 via vLLM, jumping from ~37,900 to 108,000+ tokens/sec on gemma-4-E2B-it.

✅ 100% token parity
✅ Zero quality drop
✅ Done in days, not months

selectedTweets.text:
Was curious and haven’t optimized small model on A100 before, so I tried it in Resin

125K tok/s/GPU prefill;
4K tok/s/GPU decode at 130 tok/s/user

Agent built the E2B runner from scratch. It found some neat decode optimizations at low batch too! (high batch = vllm though)

- strip assistant kv (12ms->1ms)
- fuse a bunch of cublas gelu and misc triton kernels (~1.6x decode at C=1)
- FA2 small batch planning and split-k (~11x faster)

Took about 4 hours with Astra
